blocks.text:
This journey moves between sharply different natural environments. Quito introduces the Andes, colonial architecture and the Equator. Mindo brings cloud forest, birds, butterflies and orchids. Quilotoa offers a high-altitude volcanic landscape with a lake inside the crater. In the Galápagos, the focus shifts to giant tortoises, volcanic islands, seabirds, penguins, iguanas, sea lions and snorkelling.

## What the mainland programme includes

Quito provides the historical and cultural context for your trip. Over the course of the day, you walk through the Old Town, discover the architecture of the Quito School of Art, then visit two sites associated with the Equator: Ciudad Mitad del Mundo and the Intiñán Museum.

Mindo shows you a different side of Ecuador. This compact area combines cloud forest, abundant birdlife, butterflies, orchids and outdoor activities. The programme includes a butterfly farm, a cable car above the forest, a walk and a chocolate tour.

Quilotoa takes the route back into the high Andes. The road passes through Tigua, where local artists paint colourful Andean landscapes. At the crater, you can stay at the viewpoint or walk down to the lake and, if you wish, return by mule.

## What to expect in the Galápagos

Your Galápagos visit starts on Santa Cruz Island. You can already see the changing environment on the journey from Baltra to Puerto Ayora. The island's highlands are known for giant tortoises, while excursions at sea offer opportunities to see penguins, marine iguanas, sea lions, rays, sharks and many birds.

Bartolomé combines a short climb to one of the archipelago's best-known viewpoints with time on the beach and snorkelling.

There are two possible options for Day 7. North Seymour is particularly interesting for its colonies of frigatebirds and blue-footed boobies. South Plaza has red and green sesuvium, land iguanas, sea lions and cliffs with seabirds circling overhead. The specific island is confirmed after booking.

## Transfers and guides

Transfers and excursions on mainland Ecuador are private.

An English-speaking guide or driver-guide accompanies you.

In the Galápagos Islands, transfers and excursions are shared and led by an English-speaking guide.

The final transfer from your hotel to the airport is handled by a Spanish-speaking escort; a separate excursion guide is not required.

This arrangement combines a private mainland programme with shared excursions at sea in the archipelago.
